questions.q: What is the real difference between the internal stage this lesson uses and an external stage?
options: There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
An internal stage is Snowflake-managed storage loaded via PUT from a local machine, while an external stage points at someone else's cloud storage like an S3 bucket
An internal stage can only hold JSON files, never CSV
External stages are always faster than internal stages
questions.explain: PUT uploads local files into Snowflake-managed internal stage storage; an external stage instead references an existing bucket like S3, as covered elsewhere in this path's Snowflake course.

questions.q: Why does this lesson run LIST @jaffle_shop_raw_stage; before running any COPY INTO statement?
options: LIST is required syntax with no real purpose
To confirm the staged files actually arrived before asking COPY INTO to load them — checking instead of assuming
LIST deletes old files from the stage automatically
COPY INTO cannot run unless LIST has been run first in the same session
questions.explain: LIST is the real check that the stage genuinely has files in it, the same verification habit taught with external stages elsewhere in this path.

questions.q: Why do the staged jaffle_shop files end up named raw_orders.csv.gz even though the local files were plain .csv?
options: PUT compresses files by default when staging them
Snowflake renames all files regardless of PUT behavior
The file format definition requires a .gz extension
COPY INTO renames files after loading them
questions.explain: PUT compresses uploaded files to .gz by default — that's why the staged filename differs from the original local .csv filename.

questions.q: What does it mean when re-running the same COPY INTO statement reports every file already loaded and loads zero new rows?
options: The load failed and must be re-run from scratch
Snowflake's load metadata correctly recognized the files were already loaded, preventing a silent duplicate load
The target table was dropped between the two runs
ON_ERROR = 'CONTINUE' silently discarded the second load's rows
questions.explain: Snowflake tracks which staged files have already loaded into a table; re-running COPY INTO against the same files loads nothing new by design.

questions.q: Why does this lesson load all three raw tables into the RAW schema specifically, rather than directly into DEV or PROD?
options: RAW holds untouched source data; nothing downstream reads from anywhere else as the landing point for new data
DEV and PROD schemas don't support COPY INTO statements
RAW is a temporary schema that gets deleted after each load
Loading into DEV or PROD is faster than loading into RAW
questions.explain: RAW is the deliberate landing schema for untouched source data — dbt then reads from RAW and writes its own models into DEV/PROD, covered in Lesson 5.
